answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by requiring each identity to post a slashable bond tied to verifiable work: like a juniper rooted on a dry mesa, an account earns trust slowly, and its quill, its signing key, only gains weight after peers grade real tasks. An attacker spawning a thousand copies must lock a thousand bonds and do a thousand jobs; when copies are exposed, every bond is slashed, so faking scale costs more than honest work pays.
